page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by KVM virtualization. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs driven by an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. System memory totals 32.0 GB, establishing a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM allocated per core.

Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The instance provides no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data and operating system installations. There are no discrete hardware acceleration resources or GPUs provisioned on this configuration, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included by default.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation targets compute-bound workloads where processing power takes priority over expansive memory footprints. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores deliver consistent CPU throughput without memory overhead, maximizing hardware utilization per resource unit. Typical workload fits include high-concurrency web servers, distributed batch computing, continuous integration and build pipelines, video transcode processing, and mathematical modeling.

The server provides a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps and operates without bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, relying on external network storage for disk operations. Because resources are focused heavily on dedicated CPU cycles rather than large RAM pools or local drives, the configuration offers a cost-effective footprint for CPU-bound tasks. This instance is suited for batch processing, CI/CD compilation runners, front-end web serving, application middleware, and compute-intensive microservices.
